claims.summary: In the setting of cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction (X i.i.d. uniform, Y evenly spread, L>=132, grid side about L sqrt(log N/N)/32), for exponents alpha_j in [1,infinity] with |1/alpha_1-1/alpha_2|<1/2, with probability tending to one the penalized discrepancy D_N is at least sqrt N (log N)^(3/4-(1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2)/2)/(4L_1), L_1 universal. So the bound (L/2) sqrt(N log N) fails for every L below the curve 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2=1/2, and on the curve away from its endpoints D_N >= sqrt(N log N)/(4L_1).
claims.assessment: Working proof: the monograph's Leighton-Shor construction (Section 4.8, (4.119) and (4.120)) with every tent scaled vertically by kappa=(log N)^(-|1/alpha_1-1/alpha_2|), the favorable counts used only at levels q>=r/2 for probability tending to one, smoothed over one grid cell, penalty bounded by the conjugate estimate. Concerns the discrepancy class, not matchings; endpoints of the curve not covered by this proof; whether the Ajtai-Komlos-Tusnady baseline already gives the on-curve order is unchecked.
claims.rationale: Tests the reduced statement against the known extremal construction: no refutation on the curve, where the order sqrt(N log N) is reached, and falsity below the curve.
claims.next_action: Seek an upper-bound mechanism for the class at one interior pair of the curve.

relationships: Lower bound of the conjectured order on the curve away from the endpoints, no refutation there; the class bound fails below the curve, where the conjecture makes no claim.
Class analogue of the cap for matchings, extended to every pair below the curve.
Uses its setting, grid and the class D_N.
